title: Duchy of Anhalt
capsule: Napoleon's 1806 reorganization of the Confederation of the Rhine elevated the three surviving Ascanian sub-principalities — Anhalt-Bernburg, Anhalt-Dessau, and Anhalt-Köthen — to full duchies. Köthen passed to Dessau in 1853 and Bernburg in 1863, producing a unified Duchy of Anhalt under Leopold IV with Dessau as capital. The duchy joined the North German Confederation in 1866 and the German Empire in 1871, governed under a constitutional diet of 36 members established by the fundamental law of 1859. The last duke, Joachim Ernst, abdicated in the November 1918 revolution, and Anhalt became a free state.
